## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-blind (double-anonymous): the author stays anonymous to reviewers; the author is responsible for anonymising the manuscript and files; a separate title page carries names and affiliations; authors should avoid citing themselves in a way that reveals identity (https://link.springer.com/journal/10988/submission-guidelines; the ethics page agrees, https://link.springer.com/journal/10988/ethics-and-disclosures; retrieved 2026-11-23). Manuscripts reporting primary research or secondary analysis of it have at least two referees; final accept or reject decisions can be made by an editor-in-chief or an associate editor (same guidelines page) |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. No source read |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. The pages read say nothing about publishing reports |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | SciRev, n = 2: an average of 2.0 review rounds (https://scirev.org/journal/linguistics-and-philosophy/, retrieved 2026-11-23). No journal statement |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. No reviewer-guidance page was found for this journal on the Springer pages read |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Partly. The journal's author guidelines carry a Springer Nature clause: large language models do not satisfy authorship criteria; use of an LLM should be documented in the Methods section (or a suitable alternative part); "AI assisted copy editing" (improving readability, grammar, spelling, punctuation and tone of human-written text) need not be declared (https://link.springer.com/journal/10988/submission-guidelines, retrieved 2026-11-23). A longer Springer Nature page sets a green, amber and red scheme by type of use (https://www.springernature.com/gp/policies/editorial-policies/ai-manuscript-preparation, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate found. Use is allowed with description of use and author accountability; the red category (AI as author, AI-generated scientific claims or data presented as empirical, content without verifiable source) is not permitted |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (allowed with disclosure for substantive use; same rubric as the Mind entry) |
| **Summary** | Per the publisher page: grammar, language editing, translation and summarising author-written text are green; outlines, drafting sections from author input and reference-management support are amber and must be labelled and described; replacing authorship or producing unsupervised scholarly content is red. Opaque AI-generated visuals are not permitted. The journal's guidelines add that copy-editing assistance needs no declaration. Retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Source URL** | https://link.springer.com/journal/10988/submission-guidelines ; https://www.springernature.com/gp/policies/editorial-policies/ai-manuscript-preparation |

## Format

> Source for the rules below: https://link.springer.com/journal/10988/submission-guidelines and https://link.springer.com/journal/10988/aims-and-scope, read with curl on 2026-11-23.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | "Articles, replies, or review articles" (aims-and-scope page); "The journal does not accept book reviews" (guidelines page). Special or guest-edited issues also appear (guidelines page) |
| **Word limit** | Blank. The live guidelines page contains no word or page limit (the word "words" occurs only in the abstract-length line and in a file-format sentence; checked 2026-11-23); the aims page states none. Not filled from memory |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank, since no limit is stated |
| **Abstract limit** | 150 to 250 words, with no undefined abbreviations or unspecified references; 4 to 6 keywords for indexing |
| **Reference limit** | No cap found. Citations by name and year in parentheses; the guidelines encourage APA 7 on the number of authors in reference-list entries (all authors up to 20); DOIs as full links where available; footnotes, never endnotes |
| **Supplementary material** | The guidelines carry a "Supplementary Information (SI)" section (https://link.springer.com/journal/10988/submission-guidelines, read 2026-11-23): Springer accepts multimedia and other supplementary files published online with the article; research datasets submitted as SI should follow the journal's research data policy; text files go in PDF, spreadsheets as .csv or .xlsx; files are cited in the text as "Online Resource" and each needs a caption; SI is published as received, without editing or reformatting |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Tables numbered, cited in order, with captions; Word tables rather than spreadsheets; figure resolution rules given (line art 1200 dpi, halftone 300, combination 600); colour is free online |
| **Style / submission format** | Word (.docx or .doc) or LaTeX for mathematical content with the Springer Nature template; plain 10-point Times; decimal headings with at most three levels; editable source files required at every submission and revision or the article is not considered for review; title page separate and anonymised main text; a "Statements and Declarations" section with competing interests, and a "Compliance with Ethical Standards" section where applicable; submissions without relevant declarations are returned as incomplete |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** The journal states a topical scope, not a framing rule: structure and meaning in natural language as addressed in semantics, philosophy of language, pragmatics and related disciplines, within five listed areas (https://link.springer.com/journal/10988/aims-and-scope, retrieved 2026-11-23). No requirement to cite a particular school or to position a paper against one was found.
- **What kind of engagement?** The aims place the journal at the boundary of linguistics and philosophy: its fifth area is "philosophical questions raised by linguistics as a science", including linguistics methodology, properties of linguistic theories and the relation of linguistics to other fields (aims-and-scope page). Recent titles show both formal-linguistic and philosophical-metaphysical framings, for example https://doi.org/10.1007/s10988-026-09462-2 (vagueness) and https://doi.org/10.1007/s10988-026-09472-0 (quotation).
- **Article type and length**: articles, replies and review articles; no book reviews; no word limit stated (see Format).
- **Special-issue framing seen**: a collection titled "Open Texture and Semantics" appears on recent articles (https://link.springer.com/journal/10988); its collection page (https://link.springer.com/collections/ejijgedjbi, read 2026-11-23) describes the topic as open texture and semantics, in the work of Waismann, and is marked closed for submissions; no call text with deadlines was on the page.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Blank. No source states what happens to out-of-scope submissions; SciRev shows no immediate-rejection time for this journal (https://scirev.org/journal/linguistics-and-philosophy/).

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts: regex matches over title plus abstract of OpenAlex records of this source dated 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23; 70 of 132 records have an abstract, so counts are lower bounds; shares use 70 as the denominator. Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement or a clearly dominant count. Scores measure how often a method appears in abstracts, not how a reviewer would judge it. With n = 70 one record is 1.4 percentage points, so small shares are weak evidence. The schema's rows come from the social sciences; where a row does not fit this journal it says so, and rows for linguistic and philosophical method families are added. Regexes are L1 to L22 in AI-Research Notes.

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | Authors should include, in a "Compliance with Ethical Standards" section where applicable, a statement on research involving human participants or animals and informed consent; the corresponding author should be prepared to supply documentation; editors may reject non-compliant manuscripts (https://link.springer.com/journal/10988/submission-guidelines, retrieved 2026-11-23). Experimental papers are a minority by count (5 of 70, L3) |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author papers are the majority: 81 of the 132 articles in the window (OpenAlex, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | For authors who are (temporarily) unaffiliated, the publisher captures only city and country of residence, not an email address unless requested (https://link.springer.com/journal/10988/submission-guidelines, retrieved 2026-11-23). No other independent-scholar rule found |
| **Data transparency requirement** | "Type 1" research data policy: depositing data in a public repository is encouraged, not required; for double-blind journals, blinding the authorship of data shared with reviewers is strongly suggested (https://link.springer.com/journal/10988/submission-guidelines, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double-blind: names, affiliations and acknowledgements go on a separate title page and identifying information is removed from the text and accompanying files; the author is responsible for anonymising (https://link.springer.com/journal/10988/submission-guidelines). Preprints may be posted at any time during review (https://www.springer.com/gp/editorial-policies/preprint-sharing), which can undo anonymity; the pages do not address this |
| **AI use** | LLMs are not authors; LLM use should be documented in the Methods; copy-editing assistance need not be declared (https://link.springer.com/journal/10988/submission-guidelines) |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; APC GBP 2290 / USD 3190 / EUR 2590 if open access is chosen, otherwise no charge and no page charges (https://link.springer.com/journal/10988/how-to-publish-with-us) |
| **Prior and parallel publication** | Submission implies the work is unpublished and not under consideration elsewhere; salami slicing and text recycling are named as misconduct (https://link.springer.com/journal/10988/submission-guidelines) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Scope**: the journal's scope is meaning and structure in natural language across five listed areas (Framing Requirements; https://link.springer.com/journal/10988/aims-and-scope). A paper with no connection to them is outside the stated scope.
- **Anonymisation and declarations**: the main text must be anonymised, with a separate title page, and a Statements and Declarations section is required or the submission is returned as incomplete (Practical Concerns, Format).
- **Source files**: editable source files are required at every submission and revision or the article is not considered for review (Format).
- **Prior and parallel publication**: work published or under consideration elsewhere is excluded (Practical Concerns).
- No length-related blocker can be stated: the live guidelines give no word limit (Format).

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: the publisher prints a 26-day median to first decision, while the two SciRev reports show first rounds of 17.4 and 31.1 weeks (Review Cycle Time). The figures are not reconciled; n = 2.
- **Cost**: hybrid journal; the APC is GBP 2290 / USD 3190 / EUR 2590 only if open access is chosen, and the subscription route has no charge (Open Access). Funders that require immediate open access need the OA route (https://link.springer.com/journal/10988/how-to-publish-with-us).
- **Self-archiving**: on the subscription route the accepted manuscript can be placed in repositories only after 12 months, though on a personal website at once (Preprint Policy).

### Best Suited For

- Formal semantics, pragmatics, philosophy of language and logic-oriented work on natural language: the aims list these and 26 of 70 abstract-records carry logic or modality terms, 31 pragmatics terms (Orientation, Methodological Preferences).
- Sole-authored theoretical papers: 81 of 132 articles have one author (Voice & Style).
- Replies and review articles, which the journal says it accepts (Format).

### Not Recommended For

- Corpus, fieldwork-based, interview-based or mixed-methods studies as a main route: 0 of 70 abstract-records carry these terms (Methodological Preferences). This shows absence in this window, not rejection.
- Authors who need a stated length limit or reviewer guidance in advance: neither is on the pages read (Format, Peer Review).
- Authors who need a published acceptance rate: none found (Metrics).
